column2: I check for the quiz form and its six panels, the Take quiz button, and the marking of questions 1, 2 and 3.
This part makes the quiz form. It has one panel for the score and one for each question.
I add a form called frmQuiz and put six panels on it.
Each of the six panels is named for what it holds, so the questions can go in any order.
The score panel holds the title, the score, a comment and two buttons, and question 1 holds a label, a box and Check.
Question 2 holds a label and two answer buttons, and question 3 holds a label, a picture, a list and Check.
Question 4 holds a group box with four round buttons and Check, and question 5 holds a label, a number box and Check.
This part gives the Take quiz button six lines of code. They close one form and open the other.
I meet the two new things the Take quiz button uses.
I open the code behind the Take quiz button.
Pressing Take quiz closes the data entry form and opens a new quiz form.
This part marks question 1. The typed answer is compared with the right one in small letters.
I open the code behind question 1's Check button and meet .ToLower() and BackColor.
If the typed answer in small letters matches, the score goes up and the panel turns green, or else it turns red.
I watch the question 1 panel switch off and the question 2 panel switch on.
After question 1 is marked, its panel switches off and the question 2 panel switches on.
This part marks questions 2 and 3. Question 2 has two buttons, and question 3 has a drop-down list.
I open the code behind the right answer button of question 2.
The right answer button adds 1 to the score, turns the panel green and switches on question 3.
I open the code behind the wrong answer button of question 2.
The wrong answer button turns the panel red, adds nothing, and still switches on question 3.
I open the code behind question 3's Check button.
If nothing is chosen in the question 3 list, a message asks the user to choose and nothing else happens.
If the first item in the list is chosen, the score goes up and the panel turns green.
Any other item turns the panel red, then question 3 switches off and question 4 switches on.
I open the quiz, answer in capitals, answer wrongly, try both kinds of button, and press Check with nothing chosen.
Before I code the rest of the quiz, I check I have the question 4 and 5 panels, the Return button, question 3's code and the two things in Global.cs.
This part gives the quiz a Load event, so that only question 1 can be clicked when the quiz opens.
A Load event is code that runs by itself the moment the form opens, before anyone clicks anything.
The Load event runs the moment the quiz form opens, before any click, and every form can have one.
To make a Load event I double-click the form itself, not a control on it, and Visual Studio writes frmQuiz_Load for me.
When the quiz opens, question 1 works and questions 2 to 5 are switched off and grey, so they get answered in order.
In frmQuiz_Load I set Enabled to false on the four panels and Visible to false on the Return button.
This part writes the code behind question 4's Check button: stop if nothing is chosen, mark the answer, move on to question 5.
rbB.Checked is true when B's dot is filled in, and an exclamation mark in front means NOT.
Question 4's code lives behind its Check button, and double-clicking that button in the Design tab opens the code.
Double-clicking a button in the Design tab opens the code behind that button.
If none of the four dots is filled in, the code shows a message and return stops it, so nothing else runs.
I type the if that asks whether all four dots are empty, shows a message and returns.
If the right radio button is chosen the score goes up by 1 and the group box turns green, otherwise it turns red.
After marking, question 4's panel is switched off and question 5's panel is switched on, whatever the answer was.
When question 4 is checked, its panel goes grey and question 5's panel wakes up.
When I check question 4 in my own quiz, its panel goes grey and question 5's panel wakes up.
This part writes the code behind question 5's Check button: mark the number, switch question 5 off, show the Return button.
Question 5's code lives behind its Check button, and its number is read with .Value.
nudQuestion5.Value is the number showing, and if it equals the right answer the score goes up by 1.
After question 5 is marked, its panel is switched off and the Return button is made visible.
In a working quiz the questions open in order and the Return button appears after question 5.
When I play my quiz, the questions open in order and the Return button appears after question 5.
This part writes the code behind the Return button: leave a note in Global.cs, close the quiz, open the data entry form.
The Return button's code goes behind the button, and Global.cs is where a note survives the quiz closing.
The Return button sets quizTaken to true in Global.cs, closes the quiz and opens a new data entry form.
After Return, the data entry form comes back fresh and has not read Global.cs yet, and chapter 8 fixes that.
I run the program and check each of the six things the quiz must do.
Before I start, I check the Enter button, the average button, the quiz Return button and three lines in Global.cs.
This part explains why the data entry form must read Global.cs as it opens. Then it makes the Load event.
Each time the data entry form opens it is brand new and empty, but Global.cs still holds everything.
The Load event switches every panel off, asks Global.cs three questions, then fills the boxes and switches on the right panel.
This part types the first lines of the Load event. They switch all five panels off.
I see all five panels switched off, which is how the form starts.
The first lines of the Load event switch off all five panels on the data entry form.
This part asks Global.cs three questions: quiz taken, average worked out, test taken. Each yes fills boxes and switches on a panel.
If the quiz has been taken, the score shows in black, Take quiz is hidden and the reaction test panel switches on.
When the quiz has been taken, the surname, first name, gender and year group go back from Global.cs into their boxes.
I see only the details panel switch on, for a pupil who has not taken the quiz.
If the quiz is not taken, the details panel switches on and the quiz status says Quiz not taken yet in red.
If the average is worked out, the three attempts and the average go back in their boxes and the average button hides.
I see the test panel switch off and the group panel switch on.
If the reaction test is taken, its score shows, Take test hides, its panel switches off and the group panel switches on.
I run the program and check that only the details panel works at first, and that the quiz brings the details back.
